description:
The creators of beloved children's classics often led remarkably troubled lives. From J.M. Barrie's childhood trauma and controversial relationships to Roald Dahl's tragedies and antisemitism, A.A. Milne's war-induced PTSD, Kenneth Grahame's devastating family losses, and Enid Blyton's difficult motherhood, these authors' painful experiences profoundly shaped their enduring stories for generations.
